newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rescuers clear slide area after finding survivor.
newsitem.headline: Rescuers clear slide area after finding survivor.

text.p: Rescuers on Saturday suspended efforts to pull a survivor from the rubble of a landslide at an Australian ski village after the hillside threatened to give way, police said.

Just as blankets were being passed by a human chain to an area where rescuers had heard a voice, a horn sounded warning of renewed instability in the slope and rescuers were ordered to pull back from the tonnes of debris at Thredbo village.
"Three hooters have gone off and that means everybody has to come out of the actual scene because there is a danger up there," a police spokesman said.
Reporters at the scene said rescuers had reported hearing a male voice under the rubble around dawn on Saturday. Police on Friday had virtually ruled out the chance of finding a survivor.
The landslide, which occured near midnight on Wednesday, entombed 20 people. Three deaths have been confirmed but only one body has been recovered.
Thredo, 400 km (250 miles) south of Sydney, is Australia's most popular skiing resort.
